## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Cline #13818: TUI toast wrapping — fix first-line clipping (SMALL ~1-2h)

- **What**: Toast box only set maxWidth (44 columns), so messages longer than that clipped to first line instead of wrapping. Hub update flow toasts are all longer than 44 chars — the keep-Hub reminder after Esc rendered as 'The running Cline Hub stays on the' and never reached the 'cline hub upgrade' instruction. Fix: set explicit width on the Box (message length + border + padding, capped at the previous maxWidth) so Ink's text renderer has a real edge to wrap at.
- **Why**: Multi-line instructions were silently truncated to their first line, making them unreadable and unusable. maxWidth alone is a ceiling, not a wrapping trigger — Ink needs width for wrapping.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13818 (fix(cli): make TUI toasts wrap instead of clipping after the first line)
- **Category**: command (TUI component)
- **Size**: SMALL (~1-2h — Alexi has no TUI toast component yet. When one is added, remember to set explicit width for wrapping: `<Box width={Math.min(message.length + 4, 44)}>` not just `<Box maxWidth={44}>`. Ink's Text component wraps only when the parent Box has a known width. Keep on radar for TUI surface work.)

#### 2. Cline #13727: Outdated hub drain-and-replace flow — graceful Hub upgrade (MODERATE ~4-5h, NOT applicable)

- **What**: CLI detects when it is newer than the running Hub (via build_mismatch or outdated_hub from checkManagedHubBuildMismatch) and presents a dialog: Update Now (drain + replace) or Keep Hub (dismiss, leave it running for other clients). Drain admission barrier (hub.drain RPC) is established BEFORE the busy check and retirement so no work admitted after the idle snapshot can be killed. Force requires (1) accepted drain (pre-drain builds get 404, wedged hubs timeout — both delegated to automatic idle-ensure path) and (2) user consent (dialog choice). Activity failures during the 5s drain wait window are treated as unknown (not idle), never authorize early retirement, and report still_busy if drain was accepted. Hubs rejecting drain are left to the automatic incompatible-hub path, which replaces them once idle at next startup. Dialog shows quantified session activity via describeOutdatedHubSessions (e.g. '2 active turns in 3 sessions'). Esc dismissal shows keep-Hub reminder toast (now wraps correctly per #13818). Desktop variant adds trusted-connection gate (canApproveTools) to hub_upgrade RPC.
- **Why**: Users need safe Hub upgrades that do not kill active sessions. Drain admission barrier ensures idle readings stay true through retirement. Force gate prevents accidental interruption. Activity failures as unknown (not idle) prevent transient session.list errors from authorizing premature retirement.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13727 (feat(cli): handle outdated hub sessions with drain and replace flow)
- **Category**: command (hub lifecycle)
- **Size**: MODERATE (~4-5h — Alexi is CLI-first, stateless per invocation, with file-based session storage in `~/.alexi/sessions/`. No hub daemon, no persistent orchestrator across CLI invocations, no desktop app. Cline's hub is a separate long-running process (cron runner, session multiplexer) that desktop/CLI clients connect to; Alexi's agent workflows run in GitHub Actions runners (no persistent daemon). NOT applicable to Alexi's current architecture. DEFER unless a hub-like daemon is added. If a hub enters scope, copy this pattern: (1) drain RPC before busy check, (2) force requires accepted drain + user consent, (3) treat activity failures as unknown not idle, (4) delegate undrained-idle to automatic ensure path.)

#### 3. Kilocode #13758 / Cline #13758: proto3 JSON decoding for core-connection protobus — restore enum/default-field invariants (LOW priority, standalone-server-only)

- **What**: Core-connection protobus handler (JetBrains/standalone gRPC tunnel) was dispatching parsed proto3 JSON directly to ts-proto-shaped handlers. proto3 JSON omits default-valued fields (including empty repeated fields) and encodes enums as string names; ts-proto expects numeric enums and all repeated fields present. Changing API provider threw 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading length)' in fromProtobufModelInfo, and plan/act toggle rejected its own mode. Fix: generate a per-method request-decoder map (fromJSON from ts-proto generated code) alongside the service handlers and apply it in the core-connection dispatcher before dispatch. In-process VS Code webview path unchanged (it posts structured-cloned ts-proto objects that never pass through JSON). Old standalone gRPC server restored defaults during protobuf decoding; the new tunnel skipped that step.
- **Why**: proto3 JSON shape differs from ts-proto message shape. Handlers broke on every RPC relying on repeated fields or enums. fromJSON restores the invariants.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13758, https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13758 (fix(standalone): decode core-connection protobus requests from proto3 JSON)
- **Category**: command (RPC marshalling)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP — Alexi has no JetBrains plugin, no standalone gRPC server, no core-connection tunnel, no ts-proto-generated protobus services. This is desktop-IDE-specific RPC plumbing. Not applicable to Alexi's CLI-first architecture.

#### 4. Kilocode #13760: PR badge refresh app-wide on IDE focus gain — bounded focus-driven polling (LOW priority, desktop-IDE-specific)

- **What**: JetBrains worktree PR badges only refreshed on frame focus for the project whose IdeFrame.getProject() matched the service instance, dropping activations from welcome screen (null project) and leaving second-project frames unconsumed. Combined with 30s force bar (most quick returns fell back to 90s backend PR cache), zero logging on drops, and no rate-limit suppression, real focus returns looked identical in logs to no-ops. Changes: (1) ApplicationActivationListener callbacks now unfiltered — any app activation refreshes every attached project's PR state. (2) Force bar lowered to 10s (quick browser trip to open/merge PR bypasses backend cache). (3) Spend floor (separate from bar): focus-driven forced lookup runs at most once per 30s per project; blocked return deferred as single trailing lookup (fixed deadline, strictest maxAge wins) instead of dropped. (4) Suppress focus refreshes entirely while gh RATE_LIMITED; poll remains only probe. (5) Log every drop/defer/resume/result path. Cost bounded: ~3,600 gh calls/hour worst case (alt-tab >10s/back every 30s for 1h solid) against 5,000/hour budget; rate-limit backstop cuts off before hitting limit. Deliberate refreshPr(force, maxAge) calls (post-create) unchanged (run immediately, unfloored).
- **Why**: PR badges stale on quick returns; silent drops made debugging impossible; rate exhaustion risk unbounded. 10s floor captures quick PR interactions; 30s throttle bounds cost; logging enables diagnosis.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13760 (fix(jetbrains): refresh PR badges app-wide on IDE focus gain)
- **Category**: command (IDE plugin, PR integration)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP — Alexi has no JetBrains plugin, no IDE frame focus callbacks, no PR badges. Desktop-IDE-specific polling optimization. Not applicable to CLI-first architecture.

#### 5. Kilocode #13756: Move sessions to worktree from worktree editor — agent-manager integration (LOW priority, desktop-worktree-UI)

- **What**: Base checkout's worktree editor tab now shows Move to Worktree row menu (first item, followed by separator before Rename/Delete) and New Worktree / Move to Worktree toolbar above the prompt (aligned to readable width, not full editor width), with header summarizing uncommitted changes the move would carry. WorktreeSessionEditorManager resolves once (via `git worktree list`) whether its directory is the main working tree before first session opens, gates showsBranchDock/supportsNewWorktree/supportsMoveToWorktree on that. New project-level AgentManagerHost service bridges editor to Agent Manager's move/new-worktree flows (otherwise only exist inside tool window panel); queues request and activates tool window when nothing bound yet (e.g. restored tab before tool window created). SessionActivityKind.busy() now states isBusy rule (running + question + permission) where enum can keep it exhaustive, and both row menu + chat dock read it (row menu was hiding Move only for RUNNING; chat dock hides for any isBusy).
- **Why**: Users need to move sessions to worktrees from the editor tab without switching to the tool window. busy() centralization hardens the isBusy contract.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13756 (feat(jetbrains): move sessions to a worktree from the worktree editor)
- **Category**: command (IDE plugin, agent-manager UI)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP — Alexi has no JetBrains plugin, no agent-manager worktree UI, no tool window panel, no editor tab integration. Desktop-IDE-specific UI surface. Not applicable to CLI-first architecture.

#### 6. Cline #13652 / #13657 / #13658: Hub-managed Agent Plugins support — distributed plugin architecture (HIGH complexity, DEFER — carried forward from 2026-09-03)

- **What**: Three PRs implementing Agent Plugins, a new plugin distribution model: plugins installed/enabled/disabled through Hub (central daemon), clients (desktop, CLI) discover at runtime. Core adds InMemoryMcpManager lifecycle (load manifests from installed plugin dirs, connect stdio MCP clients, expose tools/skills, disconnect on dispose), AgentPluginService (install/uninstall/list/enable/disable/update), and plugin skill toggles (whole-plugin disable persists to Hub storage, per-skill toggles rejected with error pointing to plugin toggle). CLI and desktop add `list`/`install`/`uninstall`/`enable`/`disable` commands backed by Hub RPCs. Plugins carry strict manifest schema (name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools in SKILL.md frontmatter); extra fields break parser. Auto-discovery scoped to `~/.cline/plugins/` (no system-wide paths). Stdio MCP processes await full shutdown (close stdin, drain stdout/stderr, wait for exit) so dispose() doesn't leak. Disconnect failures now caught per-server (one wedged server doesn't leak the rest), rethrown as AggregateError so upstream cleanup-error reporting still sees failure. Plugin discovery failures now logged (no silent swallow) so missing plugins are diagnosable.
- **Why**: Centralized plugin management (one install surfaces in all connected clients). Strict schema + allowlist model improves security vs uncontrolled script loading. Stdio MCP is standard plugin protocol (Anthropic, OpenAI tools teams converging). AggregateError prevents one wedged server from leaking the rest.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13652, https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13657, https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13658 (feat(core): Hub-managed Agent Plugins support, feat(cli): manage Agent Plugins through the Hub, feat(desktop): manage Agent Plugins through the Hub)
- **Category**: plugin + mcp
- **Size**: HIGH complexity ~16-20h, DEFER — Alexi already has MCP client support (`src/mcp/`) and plugin loading (`src/plugin/`), but no hub daemon, no centralized install, no desktop UI. Cline's model is desktop/hub-centric (hub daemon persists across CLI invocations; desktop app is primary UI). Alexi is CLI-first, stateless per invocation, with file-based session storage. Agent Plugins would require either (a) persistent Alexi daemon (large architecture change, out of scope), or (b) replicating plugin-install surface in CLI and storing plugin manifests in `~/.alexi/plugins/`, with per-invocation discovery (closer to Alexi's model, but still ~12h for manifest schema, install/uninstall commands, skill frontmatter parser, allowlist enforcement, stdio lifecycle). DEFER until user demand emerges or hub-like daemon added. (Carried forward from 2026-09-03.)
